description: Team VoidBrone: five Bangladeshi students building Horizon Atlas for the CLPS Lunar Mission Browser challenge. Tell us what your lander needs, and we show every Moon south pole site and date that works, and why others fail. We bring web, data and design skills. Looking for Python/SPICE and lunar science help.
summary:
Humanity is preparing to return to the Moon under the Artemis program, but landing at the lunar South Pole presents a life-or-death challenge. The Sun skims the rugged polar horizon at barely 1.5° elevation, causing crater rims to cast permanent 30+ km freezing shadows (-200°C) that starve solar panels and sever direct radio contact with Earth.

To solve this, we developed Horizon Atlas—an interactive, browser-based 3D mission planning platform. Horizon Atlas directly integrates authentic open data from the NASA JPL Horizons API (9,481 hourly Sun and Earth vectors across 13 months) and the NASA LRO LOLA 80-meter Digital Elevation Model (360° radial ray-marching up to 30 km with lunar curvature drop). 

Our multi-criteria decision engine evaluates real-time sunlight illumination, battery discharge curves, and Earth communication windows across official Artemis III candidate landing sites including Connecting Ridge, Shackleton, and Malapert Massif. 

Horizon Atlas is important because it transforms complex, inaccessible orbital software into an open, explainable web tool—empowering Artemis mission planners, researchers, and students to identify safe, survivable landing windows.
details:
1. What It Does and How It Works

Horizon Atlas is an interactive, browser-based 3D mission planning platform designed to navigate safe landing sites and optimal operational windows at the Moon's South Pole.

Unlike the lunar equator, the Sun at the lunar south pole skims the horizon at an ultra-low elevation of barely 1.5 degrees. This causes 1,000-meter crater rims to cast permanent 30-kilometer freezing shadows at minus 200 degrees Celsius, while blocking direct line-of-sight to Earth.

Horizon Atlas models this harsh environment by fusing two authentic NASA open datasets:

First, the NASA / JPL Horizons Ephemeris API, providing 9,481 hourly apparent solar and Earth azimuth and elevation coordinates across a full 13-month lunar cycle.

Second, the NASA Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter LOLA 80-meter South Polar Digital Elevation Model, ray-marched outward 360 degrees across 30 kilometers in 1-degree steps to compute realistic terrain horizon masks while rigorously accounting for spherical lunar curvature drop.

2. Benefits and Creative Innovation

- Zero Black Boxes: Every recommendation is 100% explainable from physics and geometry. Users can click any matrix cell to inspect exact solar angles, shadow entry times, and Earth communication margins.

- Interactive 3D Lunar Globe: A custom WebGL Moon globe with dynamic solar ray-casting and Artemis III landing site beacons that respond live to timeline scrubbing.

- Sensitivity and Margin Engine: Evaluates what happens if a lander touches down on a 0.3-degree local slope or micro-relief depression.

- Educational Flight Simulator Game: Translates complex astrodynamics into an intuitive playable simulator where students and engineers test battery drain curves in permanent shadow.

3. Intended Impact

Artemis astronauts and robotic landers face tight survival margins. Horizon Atlas replaces massive, expensive, and inaccessible desktop orbital software with an open, zero-install web application. It empowers Artemis mission architects, aerospace engineers, academic researchers, and students worldwide to evaluate critical mission trade-offs and discover viable lunar landing windows.

4. Tools, Coding Languages and Software

- Frontend and 3D Visualization: JavaScript (ES6+), Three.js WebGL 3D engine, HTML5 Canvas, modern CSS, and animated SVG graphics.

- Data Engineering and Pipelines: Python 3, requests for Horizons REST API query batching, rasterio, numpy, and pyproj for digital elevation model projection and radial ray-marching.

- Hosting and Infrastructure: Git, GitHub, and the Vercel Edge Network.

5. Critical Factors Considered

- Solar illumination elevation thresholds and lander battery drain limits during cold-soak darkness.

- Direct-to-Earth antenna clearance over towering crater rims.

- Spherical lunar curvature drop over 30-kilometer distances.

- High client-side performance: compressed column-array data structures allowing instant in-browser computation across 13 months of real NASA ephemerides without server latency.

6. Artificial Intelligence (AI) Tools Used

-Claude (Anthropic): Used for initial concept ideation, mathematical validation of astrodynamics formulas, and refining narrative documentation.

-Google Antigravity (Gemini): Assisted in architecting Python data pipelines for the NASA JPL Horizons API, writing the 360-degree ray-marching algorithm for the NASA LRO LOLA 80m DEM, Three.js 3D globe shader rendering, responsive UI optimization, and code refactoring.

-Note on AI Scope: All AI assistance strictly worked on public NASA open data and open-source web code, with zero proprietary or private data processed.
